messages:
Mira: Heads up — noticed a bunch of 403s in the canary for proxy-auth when SA claims are missing in the exchange path. Console shows requests as anonymous. Anyone seen this?
Sam: Seen it, looks like header folding in auth-proxy.
Alex: Can you paste the request/response headers you captured?
Mira: Sure — simplified: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer proxy-token
X-Origin-Project: proj-123
X-Auth-Claim: sa:service-A
```
Response had `x-effective-origin` missing and backend logged anonymous principal.
Jordan: We synthesize origin in two places: auth-service during token exchange and proxy when forwarding. If proxy strips the header before auth-service returns, we race and lose origin.
Pat: FYI console attribution currently prefers the `effective_origin` header, then tracing span, then token owner. That fallback order explains why we saw anonymous.
Sam: Proposed short-term: only set origin in proxy if header absent. Longer term: auth-service should emit a signed proof header so proxy can't be tricked.
Alex: Signature is safer. We could HMAC the origin using a shared key between auth-service and proxy: `X-Origin-Proof: hmac256(origin, key-id)`. cheap to verify.
Mira: Minimal patch idea in proxy:
```python
if not req.headers.get('x-origin'):
    req.headers['x-origin'] = auth_resp['origin']
```
But that still trusts client-sent headers if present.
Jordan: Right — attacker could set `x-origin`. We must reject client-supplied origin unless accompanied by `x-origin-proof` signed by auth. So rule: if `x-origin-proof` present and valid -> accept, else ignore client header and use auth response.
ops-bot: deploy-plan created: PR #2314 -> canary 10% for 1h -> monitor `console.attribution.mismatch` and `auth.exchange.latency`.
Pat: Telemetry ask: add a counter `authz.origin_source` with tags {source:auth, source:proxy, fallback:token, missing}. Also add a gauge for `console.attribution.mismatch_rate`.
Alex: UI change: console should surface both claimed origin (from header/proof) and observed origin (from tracing/token) in the attribution panel, with a tooltip explaining precedence.
Mira: Agreed. Also: quota counting must use the authoritative origin (auth-service) not the opportunistic proxy header. Otherwise charge attribution will be wrong.
Sam: We'll gate the quota switch behind a feature flag. Rollout plan: 1) add telemetry & header-proof handling; 2) proxy change to ignore unsigned origin; 3) canary; 4) flip quota flag when metrics look stable.
Jordan: I'll own telemetry metrics + console tooltip change. Will add an integration test that simulates forged header + missing proof.
Pat: I'll draft a short runbook snippet for ops: what to check when `console.attribution.mismatch` spikes (check auth logs, verify `x-origin-proof` verification failures, fallback counts).
Mira: I'll draft the proxy PR and include code for HMAC verification + unit tests. Ping reviewers in the PR for quick turnaround.
Sam: I'll review the proxy PR. Also confirm with infra about key distribution for HMAC (KMS or rotating shared secret).
Alex: Key distribution: prefer KMS-signed tokens to avoid key sync; auth-service could sign with KMS and proxy verifies using public key or via verification endpoint. That avoids secret sharing.
Mira: Nice — less ops burden. I'll note that in the PR.
ops-bot: CI: all checks pass for PR #2314.
Mira: Great. Volunteers for review?
Sam: I will review proxy changes.
Jordan: I'll review telemetry & console changes.
Pat: I'll review runbook.
Mira: Thanks all — I'll update the PR description with the rollout steps and add the canary monitor dashboard links. :thumbsup:
